title: Capability Capsule Declaration (能力胶囊)
description: The contract a capability declares. SHAPE ONLY: this file says what a field means and what type it has. It deliberately marks almost nothing as required, because required-ness lives in the gate's policy epoch, not in the schema (Protocol Buffers removed `required` for the same reason: a required field can never be taken back). Apply a profile from policy-*.json alongside this file to enforce a milestone. Schema version 2.9, 2026-09-23.

schema_version.description: The version of THIS schema the declaration is written against. Readers must accept an unknown minor and ignore fields they do not know.

identity.description: Who this capability is, and how the runtime loads it. The code is never inside a Declaration.

name.description: A stable, human-readable name. Mutable for people; the hash is what the gate binds. (Docker keeps a moving tag over an immutable digest for the same reason.)

carrier.description: WHERE THE CODE IS. The id of the thing that performs what this capsule guarantees, and the hash that id must resolve to. A capsule never contains code: it points, and the hash is how a changed head is noticed. The id is opaque here on purpose - what sort of thing it is, an MCP tool or a skill or a function, is `identity.kind`, and whatever resolves the id already knows. A capsule carries this OR `members[]`, never both: a leaf points at code, a composite holds a DAG.

ref.description: The id: an MCP tool id, a tool name, a module path, a package coordinate. Resolved by whatever loads it, not by CC.

sha256.description: What that id must hash to at load. A mismatch aborts the load.

summary.description: One line. At selection the chooser model sees this and ports, nothing more.

body.description: Every file of the capability, each with its SHA-256, so the thing checked is the thing that runs. A remote service uses `remote` instead.

remote.description: For an MCP server or A2A agent that is not local: pinned by endpoint and version. A card is metadata, never evidence.

overlays.description: Experience or prompt layers pinned per sprint. Absent means none are loaded.

ports.description: What it takes and returns, by declared type. This is what makes deterministic filtering possible, and what a merged block's boundary is derived from.

check.description: The id of the check in guarantees.checks[] that validates this output. An output with no named check cannot be gated.

needs.description: What must hold before it runs, and what it depends on.

when.description: Declared preconditions, as evaluable predicates. ONE evaluator runs these at planning and again at dispatch (predicate parity). This is the field M1 exists to deliver: today's manifests carry a name and a sentence of prose that nothing evaluates.

external.description: Capabilities, services or capsules it needs. Pinned by hash unless unpinned with a written purpose, which costs trust.

unpinned_purpose.description: Required when pinned is false. An unpinned dependency without a stated purpose is rejected.

injects.description: Keys it needs another admitted capsule to provide. Cycles across injects/provides are rejected.

model.description: Model limits. Read by model routing (M3); today no router reads anything about the capability.

changes.description: What it does to the world. The author answers for this; the gate checks the declaration against what is observed.

undo.description: How it is undone, or an explicit statement that it cannot be. Registrations come back out; emissions and external state do not.

guarantees.description: What it claims, and how each claim is checked. Every check has a target because the declaration gives it one.

target.description: The port or invariant this check is about.

anchor.description: What the check is anchored to.

author.description: Who wrote the check. Never the builder, for a certified capsule.

written_before_body.description: True when the check existed before the body it tests, which is what binds a suite to the contract.

held_out.description: True when the check is held out of what the builder could see.

signal_source.description: Where the pass or fail signal comes from. A capsule-sourced signal is never admission evidence.

owner.description: Self-owned checks are permitted, but are never evidence (SCHEMA.md 4.4).

assurance.description: How strongly the check is backed: enforced > tested > audited > declared.

quality.description: Quality is a RATE OVER A WINDOW, never a verdict. Below min_observations the claim is `unmeasured`, and unmeasured is never silently treated as passing (Envoy computes no verdict below its request volume; SonarQube waives coverage under 20 new lines; Kayenta gives no-data its own class).

judge.description: A judge is never itself a capsule.

exempt.description: Exempts a capsule from the library's verification policies. Generalists only, and more than one generalist may exist.

members.description: THE SET CASE. A capsule holds a set of capabilities; n = 1 is the degenerate case and omits this field. Members are pinned by hash, so a block's internals cannot move under it. Composition runs its members in order, UNCHANGED: it buys placement grain and a block-level quality record, not execution saving.

structure.description: The internal DAG of a composite, in the shape symphony/flow already uses for a distilled recipe.

wiring.description: COMPOSITES ONLY. How the members are put together, one wire per connection. SCHEMA.md 3.x specifies `wiring[] {from, to}`, and the gate checks that wires connect compatible types (4.10), so the field has to exist here or a conforming composite is rejected. An endpoint is `<role>.<port>` for a member's port, or `inputs.<port>` / `outputs.<port>` for the composite's own boundary, which is what makes one capsule usable INSIDE another: the outer ports are wired to inner ones rather than redeclared.

from.description: `inputs.<port>` of this capsule, or `<role>.<port>` of a member that produces it.

to.description: `outputs.<port>` of this capsule, or `<role>.<port>` of a member that consumes it.

evolution.description: WHAT THIS CAPSULE PROMISES TO KEEP STABLE, and what the author wants a reviser to know. Framed as a promise rather than as a permission, because that is what the rest of this schema does: the capsule states what it will hold to, and RSI reads its search space off that. Nothing here forbids an edit. `contract_hash` already makes every edit visible, and a body submitted against a changed contract voids the suite written for it.

frozen.description: Parts of the contract this capsule promises not to move. Changing one is declaring a NEW capability, not a better version of this one, so a revision that moves a frozen part takes `relation: supersedes` and a new name rather than replacing this one in place. Inside `contract_hash`, because changing the promise changes the contract.

notes_for_builder.description: ADVISORY ONLY, from the author to whoever revises this, RSI included. Never evidence, never gating, and read by no check. Outside `contract_hash`, so editing a note does not void a suite. Anything that must hold belongs in `needs`, `changes` or `guarantees`, where something can check it.

coverage.description: What the builder knowingly leaves out. Specified in SCHEMA.md 3.1 from v2.3 and never implemented here, so a declaration written to spec was rejected. Outside `contract_hash`.

undeclared_notes.description: What is deliberately not declared, and why. The screener treats a capsule that says so differently from one that simply omits it.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256. Identity is the hash of the artifact, never of the derivation.

effect_class.description: Composition keys off this: pure and idempotent compose freely, compensable compose with the undo path tracked, irreversible or undeclared are gated.

lineage.description: Where it came from. CC stores and exposes this; RSI chooses what to branch from. Joined to RSI's own tree by builder_ref.

relation.description: How this capsule relates to its parent. `composes` is a block built from members that run UNCHANGED. `fuses` is reserved for a future operation that rewrites a block's internals so its members run in one pass; it is NOT implemented, and nothing in 2.9 depends on it.

predicate.description: An evaluable precondition. `check` names it; `path`, `op` and `value` make it runnable by the shared evaluator. A predicate with only `check` and `description` is prose, which is exactly what exists today and what M1 replaces.

evaluable_at.description: planning: the filter can read it. dispatch: only fresh state can answer it. both: parity is testable.

on_unknown.description: Fail closed by default: unknown defers or blocks, never passes.

allOf.title: A capsule is either a leaf or a composite, never both
allOf.$comment: members[] means the work is a DAG of other capsules. identity.carrier means the work is done by code this capsule points at. Both at once has no meaning.
